title: A smaller first-home deposit
who: Eligible first-home buyers using a participating lender.
before: The earlier guarantee scheme had income limits and capped places.
after: The expanded Australian Government 5% Deposit Scheme has no income caps or limit on places. Eligible borrowers can avoid LMI; property price caps and lender checks still apply.
nextStep: Check your savings after buying costs, the property's location cap and your eligibility before planning around a 5% deposit.

title: Capital gains tax rules are changing
who: Investors affected by the new CGT arrangements, including individuals and trusts.
before: The existing 50% discount can apply to eligible capital gains after the required holding period.
after: Legislated reforms replace that discount with inflation adjustments and a minimum 30% tax on real gains arising from 1 July 2027. Transitional rules and exceptions, including a choice for eligible new builds, matter.
nextStep: Keep purchase, improvement and sale records. Do not apply a flat 50% discount to a future sale without checking the applicable rules.
sources: Federal Register: Tax Reform No. 1 Act 2026
Treasury: CGT and negative gearing explainer

title: Rental losses: the purchase date matters
who: Investors whose contract to buy established residential property was entered into at or after 7:30 pm AEST on 12 May 2026.
before: Under existing rules, eligible rental losses can generally reduce other taxable income.
after: From 2027–28, affected losses can offset residential property income, with unused losses carried forward, rather than wages. Earlier holdings, eligible new builds and other exceptions have different treatment.
nextStep: Check when your purchase contract was entered into, rather than the settlement date, plus the property type and transition rules before estimating any tax benefit.
sources: Federal Register: Tax Reform No. 1 Act 2026
Treasury: CGT and negative gearing explainer

title: Foreign buyers: established-home restriction
who: People treated as foreign investors under the federal rules.
before: Earlier guidance described a restriction ending on 31 March 2027.
after: Treasury's guidance, updated 1 July 2026, states the restriction runs to 30 June 2029. Foreign investors are generally prohibited from buying established homes, with limited exceptions.
nextStep: Check the current Treasury guidance and approval requirements before signing. State surcharges are a separate check.
